Historical observations for this pairing come from tide gauges, which are devices that measure sea level relative to the shoreline. Many coastal cities have had working tide gauges for a half-century or more.

Projections are scenarios that were published by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 2017. The trajectories are based on a variety of observed and modeled studies. NOAA published newer scenarios in 2022, but those scenarios present return intervals and number of “events,” which could last for more than one day and thus cannot be translated simply into a number of days to align with the observed record.

The feature tracks the number of days per year when each tide gauge measures water that was higher than a local flooding threshold determined by NOAA. Flood thresholds are defined based on a statistical approach that accounts for typical local fluctuations in the tides. This feature excludes a few locations where thresholds were recently upgraded, as it would have resulted in the projections and observations applying different thresholds.
